SIO-001: On completing this stop, the learner will be able to introduce themselves and a third person (*Je m'appelle…*, *Il/Elle s'appelle…*), ask someone's name with both *tu* (*Comment tu t'appelles ?*) and *vous* (*Comment vous vous appelez ?*), and conjugate *s'appeler* across all 8 subject forms drilled in the deck (*je* → *elles*), with at least 5/6 correct. (*M./Mme* as forms of address is assessed under SIO-006, where its content lives.)
SIO-002: Given the 12 interlocutors in the deck (*un copain*, *le professeur*, *une vendeuse*…), the learner will classify each under the appropriate pronoun — *tu*, polite singular *vous*, or plural *vous* — in at least 10 of the 12. (The reason for each choice is revealed as feedback after the attempt; the learner selects, and is not asked to produce a justification.)
SIO-003: The learner will name all 26 letters of the French alphabet, sort them into the 7 vowel-sound groups (ah · ay · air · i · ü · oh · uh), and spell a given word aloud with at least 90% of the letters correct, asking or answering *Comment ça s'écrit ?*
SIO-004: The learner will list the 7 days of the week in order and the 3 moments of the day (*matin, après-midi, soir*), classify any given day as weekday or weekend, and ask and answer *C'est quand ?*
SIO-005: The learner will name the 12 colours in French and give the matching mnemonic object (*le feu rouge*, *le flamant rose*…) for at least 10 of the 12.
SIO-006: Given the 18 core nouns (*un prénom* … *un micro*), the learner will label at least 15 with the correct article *un/une*, answer *C'est où ? / C'est qui ? / C'est quoi ?* appropriately for a given place, person, or object, and choose *Monsieur (M.)* or *Madame (Mme)* as the form of address for a given person.
SIO-007: The learner will read aloud and say any number from 0 to 20, explain 17–19 as composites (*dix-sept* = 10 + 7), say 20, and answer *Il y a combien d'étudiants ?*
SIO-008: On hearing any of the 9 classroom instructions (*Écoutez !, Regardez !, Répétez !, Lisez !, Écrivez !, Parlez !, Notez !, Comptez !, Associez !*), the learner will perform the correct action for at least 8 of the 9, and will ask *On fait quoi ?* when unsure what to do.
SIO-009: Given a time of day and a relationship (casual or formal), the learner will produce a register-appropriate greeting or leave-taking in at least 8 of 10 prompts, and sort greeting phrases into meeting vs parting and universal vs familiar.
SIO-010: The learner will carry out a complete first-time meeting in French, performing every step of the chain without omission: greet, ask a name (with *tu* or *vous*), give their own name, ask *Et toi ?*, ask and answer *Comment ça s'écrit ?*, say *Enchanté(e)*, and take leave with *Au revoir !*
SIO-011: The learner will identify each of the 8 stressed pronouns (*moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles*) by its position — after a preposition, after *c'est*, or standing alone — and match at least 7 of the 8 to their subject pronouns.
SIO-012: The learner will name 10 professions in both masculine and feminine forms and present a person's job with *il est / elle est ___* or *C'est un/une ___* correctly for at least 8 of the 10.
SIO-013: The learner will name academic subjects with the correct article, ask *Qu'est-ce que tu étudies ?*, and answer with *Je suis étudiant(e) en ___*.
SIO-014: The learner will conjugate *être* in all 8 persons with at least 7/8 correct and apply gender and number agreement to *étudiant / étudiante / étudiants / étudiantes*.
SIO-015: The learner will name 25 countries with the correct article (*le, la, l', les*, or no article) for at least 20 of the 25, and ask *C'est quel pays ?*
SIO-016: For the 25 countries, the learner will produce the nationality adjective in all 4 forms (m.sg, f.sg, m.pl, f.pl) and link country to nationality for at least 20 of the 25.
SIO-017: The learner will match each of the 25 countries to the language(s) spoken there, using *on parle ___*, for at least 20 of the 25.
SIO-018: The learner will read aloud and say any number from 20 to 69, identify the 6 tens, and build the composites 21–69 — with *et un* where required — at 90% accuracy or better.
SIO-019: The learner will conjugate *avoir* with at least 7/8 correct, state an age with *J'ai ___ ans*, and sort the deck's 11 states into their two families with at least 5/6 correct: *avoir* + noun (*faim, soif, chaud, froid, envie, besoin*) vs *être* + adjective (*fatigué, content, malade, triste, calme*), applying singular/plural agreement to the *être* adjectives. (Negative forms are not drilled in this stop's content — negation is built at SIO-028.)
SIO-020: With time to prepare, the learner will write 3–4 comprehensible sentences presenting a francophone country, including all 4 required elements: name, location, language, and one cultural fact.
SIO-021: The learner will present at least 6 of the 14 everyday objects (*un sac* … *une clé*) using *c'est + un/une + N* and *ce sont + des + N*, and ask *C'est quoi ?*
SIO-022: Given at least 8 prompts, the learner will select the possessive adjective (*mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses, notre/votre/leur/leurs*) that agrees with the gender and number of the noun possessed — not the owner — with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-023: The learner will conjugate *aimer* in all persons and express likes with both *aimer* + definite article + noun (*J'aime le cinéma*) and *aimer* + infinitive (*J'aime lire*), producing at least 2 examples of each pattern.
SIO-024: The learner will say what sports and activities they do using *faire* with the correct article contraction (*du / de la / de l' / des*) for at least 6 activities, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-025: The learner will ask *Pourquoi ?* and give a simple reason for a preference with *parce que c'est* + adjective or *parce que j'aime* + noun, for at least 3 prompts.
SIO-026: The learner will say where they go using *aller* with the correct article contraction (*au / à la / à l' / aux*) for at least 6 destinations, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-027: The learner will say when they do their regular activities using *le* + day, *le week-end*, *tous les jours/soirs/matins*, and *à* + clock time (*à 8 heures, à midi, à minuit*) for at least 5 prompts, and sort the expressions into day, frequency, and clock time.
SIO-028: The learner will negate with *ne … pas* using the correct article family: *pas de/d'* after *faire*, *il y a*, and quantities (*Je ne fais pas de tennis*), while keeping *le/la/les* after *aimer*, *adorer*, and *détester* (*Je n'aime pas le tennis*).
SIO-029: In a short dialogue, the learner will use *vouloir/pouvoir* to perform all 4 functions: invite (*Tu veux venir ?*), accept (*Je veux bien !*), refuse (*Je ne peux pas*), and reschedule (*On peut se voir samedi ?*).
SIO-030: With time to prepare, the learner will produce the well-wish formulas (*Bon anniversaire !, Bonne chance !, Bon voyage !, Bonne année !, Bonne fête !*) and write a 4–6 sentence holiday email using at least 3 of the connectors *d'abord, ensuite, aussi, mais, et, enfin* correctly.
SIO-031: The learner will describe the weather using at least 6 expressions (*Il fait beau/chaud/froid/mauvais, il pleut, il neige, il y a du vent/du soleil/des nuages*) with at least 80% accuracy, and ask *Quel temps fait-il ?*
SIO-032: The learner will say which country they are in, going to, or coming from, using *en/au/aux/à* with *être*, *aller*, and *venir* in at least 6 sentences, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-033: The learner will say where they are, where they are going, and where they are coming from around town, using *être/aller/venir* with the correct contraction (*au/à la/à l'/aux, du/de la/de l'*) in at least 6 sentences, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-034: The learner will say where a place is in relation to another using the spatial prepositions *à côté de, en face de, près de, loin de* with the correct article contraction, for at least 4 prompts.
SIO-035: The learner will form a yes/no question with *Est-ce que… ?* and with intonation, and an open question with each of the 7 question words (*Où, Quand, Comment, Pourquoi, Qu'est-ce que, Qui, Combien de*), with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-036: The learner will ask for and give directions without using the imperative, producing the *vous* + present pattern the deck drills (*Vous allez tout droit. / Vous tournez à gauche. / Vous prenez la première rue à droite. / C'est au bout de la rue.*) and understanding the same itinerary steps in the *il faut* + infinitive and *on* + present variants met in the reading texts (*il faut prendre la deuxième rue à gauche / on va tout droit jusqu'au carrefour*); the learner will use the ordinals *première* and *deuxième* — the only ordinals this stop's content shows — in street directions, correctly for at least 4 prompts at 80% or better.
SIO-037: The learner will conjugate *pouvoir* in its key persons and produce at least 3 statements about what is possible or allowed in a place, or requests for permission, using *on peut / je peux / vous pouvez* + infinitive.
SIO-038: The learner will ask how someone gets somewhere (*Comment tu vas à l'école ?*), answer with *prendre* + mode of transport, and use the pronoun *y* (*J'y vais en bus. / On y va ?*) in at least 3 sentences.
SIO-039: The learner will express wants and needs politely using all 5 frames the deck teaches — *je voudrais, j'aimerais, j'ai envie de, j'ai besoin de, je veux* — each followed by a noun or an infinitive, as drilled in the deck's two examples per frame.
SIO-040: The learner will explain step by step how to get somewhere, describing at least 4 ordered steps linked with *d'abord, puis, ensuite, après, enfin/finalement*, using *il faut* + infinitive or *on* + present (no imperative) combined with transport and direction vocabulary.
SIO-041: The learner will name the 4 meals (*petit-déjeuner, déjeuner, goûter, dîner*) and at least 2 foods or drinks for each, and say what they eat and drink at each meal, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-042: The learner will distinguish liking (*J'aime le pain* — definite) from consuming (*Je mange du pain* — partitive) in at least 8 prompts with at least 80% accuracy, rewrite at least 5 negatives with *de/d'* (*Je ne mange pas de viande*), use quantity expressions with *de/d'* (*beaucoup de pain, assez de sel, trop de sucre, un peu de lait, un kilo de pommes*) as the deck's quantities category drills, and conjugate *manger* and *boire* in all persons with at least 7/8 correct for each.
SIO-043: The learner will describe habits using the 5 frequency adverbs (*toujours, souvent, parfois, rarement, ne… jamais*), placing the adverb correctly after the verb in at least 5 sentences, and order the adverbs on a frequency scale.
SIO-044: The learner will match at least 5 food shops (*boulangerie, épicerie, boucherie, marché, supermarché*) to what they sell, say where they shop, ask *Combien ça coûte ?* and *Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît*, and handle a market exchange on either side of the stall: assign each line of the dialogue to *le marchand* or *le client*, put the exchange in order, and produce *Je voudrais…*, *Ça fait combien ?*, and *Et avec ceci ?*
SIO-045A: The learner will count from 70 to 99 following the *soixante-dix* and *quatre-vingts* patterns, and understand and produce these numbers in market prices (*Ça fait quatre-vingt-cinq euros.*).
SIO-046: The learner will point out specific items when shopping or ordering by selecting *ce/cet/cette/ces* correctly by gender and number (*ce pain, cet ananas, cette tarte, ces légumes*) for at least 8 nouns, with at least 80% accuracy.
SIO-047: The learner will say what they are going to do — today, this weekend, after class — producing at least 5 futur-proche sentences with correctly conjugated *aller* + infinitive (*Je vais manger. / Nous allons visiter le marché.*).
SIO-048: The learner will give at least 5 pieces of simple advice about food, health, and daily life using *tu dois* + infinitive (personal obligation), *il faut* + infinitive (general necessity), and *tu peux* + infinitive (suggestion), with correct verb forms (*Tu dois dormir plus. / Il faut manger des légumes. / Tu peux prendre le bus.*).
SIO-049: The learner will give a simple restaurant review stating at least 1 positive point (*C'est délicieux !*), at least 1 negative point (*Le service est lent.*), and a clear recommendation (*Je recommande / Je ne recommande pas*).
SIO-050: The learner will get through a complete restaurant visit in role-play, performing all 6 steps: greet the waiter, read the menu, order (*entrée/plat/boisson/dessert*), interact during the meal, ask for the bill, and pay and say goodbye.
